terms.RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: technique where an LLM retrieves relevant content from an external knowledge store before generating a response
terms.LLM: Large Language Model: a neural network trained on large text corpora capable of generating, understanding, and reasoning over natural language
terms.MCP: Model Context Protocol: open standard for connecting LLMs to external tools, data sources, and services via a common interface
terms.agent: An LLM-powered system that can perceive its environment, plan multi-step actions, and call tools to accomplish a goal autonomously
terms.agentic: Describing AI workflows where the model drives multi-step planning and tool use rather than responding to a single prompt
terms.token: The basic unit of text processed by an LLM, roughly corresponding to a word or subword; LLMs are billed by token count
terms.fine-tuning: Continued training of a pre-trained model on a domain-specific dataset to specialize its outputs
terms.RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: technique for aligning LLM outputs with human preferences via reward models
terms.SFT: Supervised Fine-Tuning: training a model on labeled (prompt, response) pairs as a first alignment step
terms.context window: The maximum number of tokens an LLM can process in a single forward pass; determines how much text the model can 'see' at once
terms.hallucination: When an LLM generates factually incorrect or fabricated information stated with apparent confidence
terms.prompt: The input text given to an LLM; prompt engineering involves crafting inputs to elicit desired outputs
terms.Claude Code: Anthropic's terminal-based agentic coding assistant that runs Claude models and can read, write, and execute code in the user's environment
terms.skill: In Claude Code and Pi: a reusable markdown file defining a workflow or behavior that agents invoke as a named command
terms.plugin: In Claude Code: an installable package of skills, agents, rules, and MCP tools that extend the base agent's capabilities
terms.subagent: A specialized agent spawned by a coordinator agent to handle a specific subtask in parallel or in sequence
terms.hook: In Claude Code: a shell command configured to run automatically on lifecycle events such as PostToolUse or PreCommit
terms.CLAUDE.md: Project-level configuration file read by Claude Code at the start of each session; defines rules, workflows, and project context
terms.AGENTS.md: Alternative name for the agent configuration file (equivalent to CLAUDE.md in some harnesses)
terms.knowledge graph: A graph-structured representation of entities (nodes) and relationships (edges) that enables relational queries over facts
terms.knowledge base: A structured store of information that an agent reads from and writes to, persisting knowledge across sessions
terms.LLM Wiki: Andrej Karpathy's pattern for an LLM agent that incrementally builds and maintains a markdown wiki from raw sources, compiling knowledge rather than re-deriving it per query
terms.Obsidian: A markdown-based personal knowledge management app that uses [[wiki-links]] for note interconnection; the viewer for this wiki
terms.obsidiantools: Python library for programmatic analysis of Obsidian vaults: backlinks, wikilink parsing, orphan detection
terms.pipeline: A sequence of processing steps where the output of each step feeds the next; used here for the wiki ingestion workflow
terms.GGUF: A binary file format for quantized LLM weights, used by llama.cpp and compatible inference engines
terms.quantization: Reducing the numeric precision of model weights to lower memory usage and increase inference speed, at some cost to accuracy
terms.speculative decoding: Inference acceleration technique using a small draft model to propose tokens that the large model then verifies in parallel
terms.test-time compute: Extra computation applied at inference time (rather than training time) to improve model outputs, e.g. chain-of-thought, self-consistency, or search
terms.KV cache: Key-Value cache: stored intermediate attention computations that allow incremental token generation without recomputing past context
terms.HLE: Humanity's Last Exam: a benchmark of extremely hard academic questions used to evaluate frontier model reasoning capabilities
terms.MATH-500: A benchmark of 500 competition-level mathematics problems used to evaluate LLM reasoning and problem-solving
terms.Lean 4: A formal mathematics proof assistant and programming language; used to evaluate LLM theorem-proving capabilities
terms.self-play: Training technique where a model improves by playing against itself or generating its own training signal
terms.Conjecturer: In self-play for theorem proving: the agent that generates new problem statements for the Solver to attempt
terms.DAG: Directed Acyclic Graph: a graph structure with no cycles, used in PARNESS to represent declarative workflow pipelines
terms.arXiv: Open-access preprint server for scientific papers in physics, mathematics, computer science, and related fields
terms.NeurIPS: Neural Information Processing Systems: a top-tier academic conference on machine learning and AI
terms.EMNLP: Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: a top-tier NLP/LLM research conference
terms.GitHub Copilot: Microsoft/GitHub's AI coding assistant integrated into VS Code, JetBrains, and other IDEs; uses OpenAI models
terms.Codex: OpenAI's coding-focused model and product (also the name of their terminal-based coding agent)
terms.OpenCode: Open-source terminal coding agent supporting multiple LLM providers
terms.CHORUS: Multi-model code review tool that orchestrates Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Kimi in parallel using existing subscriptions
terms.bilingual: In this wiki: every entry contains both an English section and a Russian section in the same .md file
terms.cursor: In reddit scanning: the last-seen post ID stored per subreddit to enable incremental fetching of only new posts
terms.Mythos: Claude Mythos Preview: Anthropic frontier model above Opus, focused on cybersecurity; first AI to complete a full 32-step corporate network attack simulation
terms.harness: The scaffolding around an LLM: context assembly, tool exposure, agent loop, and evaluation logic — everything except the model weights themselves
terms.harness engineering: The discipline of designing and iterating on the scaffolding (harness) that turns a raw LLM into a reliable working agent
terms.SGS: Self-Guided Self-Play: LLM training technique adding a Guide role to prevent Conjecturer collapse in self-play loops
terms.WIP=1: Work In Progress limit of one: discipline of giving an agent exactly one active task at a time, preventing context fragmentation
terms.Agent OS: Agent Operating System: infrastructure that manages AI agents the way an OS manages processes, providing scheduling, memory, tools, identity, observability, and guardrails
terms.ARR framework: Atomic + Reliable + Reversible: three properties a task must have for an AI agent to handle it reliably
terms.OODA loop: Observe-Orient-Decide-Act: decision cycle originally from military strategy, applied to AI agent reasoning loops
terms.TTFT: Time To First Token: latency from prompt submission to receipt of the first generated token; key metric for interactive AI applications
terms.Orthrus: Hybrid diffusion+autoregressive architecture for LLM inference acceleration; injects a trainable diffusion module into a frozen AR transformer to achieve ~7.8× throughput
terms.Sparky: Fully offline AI robot built in a suitcase: Jetson Orin NX Super + Gemma 4 E4B, 30+ sensors, zero cloud dependency
terms.Poetiq: AI coding harness using recursive self-improvement to achieve SOTA coding benchmark performance beyond frontier model baselines
terms.distillation loop: The Plan→Execute→Distill→Commit cycle for accumulating project knowledge in git; the distill step extracts only reusable knowledge into playbooks
terms.session entropy: Degradation of agent effectiveness over a session due to accumulated unclean state, half-applied changes, and context drift
terms.cold-start test: A test that verifies an agent can pick up a task from a fresh context with no prior session memory; validates harness self-containment
terms.Prompt Contract: A structured prompt framework with four required fields: Goal, Constraints, Format, and Failure (what to do when blocked)
terms.AgentMemory: Open-source persistent memory layer for coding agents; 51-tool MCP server with semantic + episodic memory tiers, 95.2% R@5 recall
